title: Randy's Donuts Opens Across From Beloved Stan's, Sparking Santa Clara's Doughnut Showdown
excerpt: The iconic Los Angeles chain planted its first Bay Area location directly opposite a 65-year-old family institution, turning a quiet stretch of Homestead Road into Silicon Valley's sweetest battleground.
body:
• Randy's Donuts opened its first Bay Area location on August 1 at 2595 Homestead Road in Santa Clara, directly across from Stan's Donut Shop, a family-owned institution since 1959.
  • The franchise, operated by Sweet Rings LLC and led by owner Ausaf Masud, is Randy's 28th location after expanding from its iconic Inglewood flagship across Southern California, Las Vegas, Arizona, and Georgia.
  • Stan's Donut Shop, founded by World War II veteran Stanford Wittmayer, is still family-run and celebrated for its glazed doughnuts and vintage diner atmosphere.
  • Both sides and longtime customers say the two shops can coexist, framing the proximity as healthy competition in a doughnut-loving neighborhood.

An LA Icon Lands in Silicon Valley

Randy's Donuts, the Los Angeles chain famous for the giant doughnut perched atop its original Inglewood location, opened its first Bay Area shop on Friday at 2595 Homestead Road in Santa Clara. The store gave away free doughnuts from 7 a.m. to noon, with the first 25 customers in line receiving a complimentary half-dozen box.

The new location sits directly across the street from Stan's Donut Shop, a South Bay institution that has drawn loyal customers—and long lines—since 1959. The deliberate proximity has turned a quiet stretch of residential Santa Clara into what locals are calling a doughnut war zone.

But Ausaf Masud, one of the owners of Sweet Rings LLC, the franchise group bringing Randy's to the area, does not see it that way.

"People over here are aware of donuts. Benefits each one of us. It's a very nice competitive edge now. People get to choose which one they want to try, which one they wanna like. That builds some new taste buds."

— Ausaf Masud, owner, Sweet Rings LLC

Stan's: A Silicon Valley Institution

Stan's Donut Shop was established in April 1959 by Stanford Wittmayer, a World War II veteran, and his wife Florence, known to family and friends as Tina. For decades, their son Richard worked alongside his father, learning the recipes and eventually taking over the business. Today, several of the Wittmayer children continue the operation, with head baker Jesus Lopez, trained by Rick Wittmayer, maintaining the family's methods.

The shop at 2628 Homestead Road, across from Central Park Library, retains its vintage diner look: long counter seating, handwritten signs, and a limited-run menu that regularly sells out before closing time. Its warm glazed doughnuts, baked fresh and served straight off the fryer, have earned a 4.9 rating on TripAdvisor with over 200 reviews, along with a wall of framed press accolades spanning generations.

Stan's closes early—by 2:30 p.m.—and the demand-driven scarcity is part of its cult appeal.

Randy's Brings Hollywood Pedigree

Randy's Donuts, founded in 1952, is a different animal. Its giant rooftop doughnut sign became a pop-culture landmark after appearing in films like Iron Man 2 and being parodied in Friday. The chain has expanded to 27 locations before Santa Clara, spanning Southern California, Las Vegas, Arizona, and Georgia.

The Santa Clara menu mixes traditional favorites like glazed rings with specialty flavors including matcha, churro, and seasonal offerings like mango tajín. The location has indoor and outdoor seating and plans for a drive-through later.

Coexistence, Not War

Longtime residents appeared more amused than alarmed by the matchup.

"I've lived here since 1978. I love Stan's Donuts. The only complaint I have about Stan's Donuts is that it closes a little bit early. I think it'd be nice to have a little competition and maybe different varieties."

— Leonard Armenta, Santa Clara resident

Armenta added that he believes both businesses "will peacefully exist like we all should."

For the large Indian diaspora in Silicon Valley—Santa Clara sits at the heart of a region with one of the highest concentrations of Indian-Americans in the country—the doughnut showdown adds to a neighborhood already rich in food options. The franchise owner's name, Ausaf Masud, and the South Asian presence in the area underscore how immigrant entrepreneurship continues to shape the Bay Area's food landscape, one glazed ring at a time.
